requiredFindings.location: crates/platform/src/filesystem/directory_publication.rs, create_private_directory_stage and the two accessor docs
requiredFindings.finding: create_private_directory_stage dups the caller's parent into its own RetainedDirectory, so stage.parent_directory() and the publication's are a DIFFERENT handle object wrapping a dup of the same fd. runtime32's DirectoryBarrierReceipt::is_for is deliberately handle-object identity, so it answers false across the two (probe P1). This module's own doc requires the caller to keep its original fence through the required parent barrier, yet a receipt taken on the caller's handle cannot be shown through the public API to concern the parent this publication used: there is no public directory-identity comparison between two RetainedDirectory values. Two correct implementations could barrier different handles and neither could prove the association.
requiredFindings.required: Document the relationship (the parent is a dup; a runtime32 receipt on the caller's handle will not is_for the publication's), or expose a way to compare the publication's parent with a caller-held handle. Documentation is sufficient; a new comparison would need its own review.

requiredFindings.finding: The doc states 'The original syscall error is retained when both rename and post-check fail' but says nothing about the opposite direction: when the rename SUCCEEDS and the post-check fails, the caller receives the post-check's error with Indeterminate and no indication that the rename succeeded. The behaviour is right, but this is the same class of undocumented precedence raised as RF-3 against source393 and closed in source395 by stating both directions.
requiredFindings.required: State that when the rename succeeds and the post-check fails, the post-check's error is returned and the successful rename is not reported.

requiredFindings.finding: Unchanged is reachable only from a pre-syscall refusal or from AlreadyExists with the original stage still bound. Every other rename errno, including definitionally pre-effect ones such as ENAMETOOLONG (probe P2: nothing published, stage intact, yet Indeterminate), is reported uncertain. Conservative is the right default, but the cost is unstated: under the creation law this primitive is built for, Indeterminate latches the invocation, so a final component longer than NAME_MAX burns the whole attempt instead of yielding a clean request rejection. The module's 1023-byte grammar is deliberately not a NAME_MAX oracle, consistent with the grammar-versus-kernel separation established in source389.
requiredFindings.required: Say that Indeterminate covers refusals that could in principle be known pre-effect, and that the caller owes its own platform name-length admission.

observations.note: failure consumes the stage, there is no Drop cleanup, and the type cannot be reconstructed from a name, nonce or existing directory. Measured in P6: every failed publish deterministically leaves one directory the same process can no longer address through this API, so a retry loop leaks one stage per attempt. Each part is disclosed; the combination is not, and owner397 §6 already anticipates a separately specified cleanup mechanism.
mkdirat mode 0o700 is subject to umask and inherited ACLs, as documented; the unit observes the resulting mode in its own test but cannot enforce it, while the owner law requires 0700 exactly.
the parent nlink()==0 arm in recheck() carries the same macOS caveat runtime32 documented: a positive link count is not attachment. Consistent with probe P3.
O_NONBLOCK on the directory open is harmless alongside O_DIRECTORY; recorded only so it is not mistaken for a behavioural requirement.
the fault seam publish_with is private and production passes exactly one closure, so no public caller can substitute the syscall — the same discipline as confirm_directory_with in runtime32.
tests run on the pinned TMPDIR volume (APFS), not a prospective installation-root volume, and are macOS-only in effect; no Linux, crash, power-loss or profile qualification is claimed or checked.
